title: GPT-6 Astra Just Dropped and Reviewers Already Cooking Insane AI Games
author: JoseQuanGT
selftext:

Still extremely impressive, but still, it's the one-shot experience. It will build something neat and cohesive, often by repurposing existing assets. But the moment you want to change, add, or refine something, it becomes a real slog.

I just added a flyout menu to my app and had to requery it like 10 times just to get the layering right. Obviously, this was with 5,6 on high, and maybe Astra is miles ahead. The DeepSWE benchmarking does certainly indicate that it is better at real/independent/non-cheaty coding.

comments.author: daddywookie
comments.body:
I kinda hate this type of content. It looks cool but it breaks my heart a little as a keen amateur. It is an asset flip on steroids.

It makes all the effort I am putting into slowly crafting my own game feel utterly pointless when anybody can just say “make me a game” and get it looking like this.

replies.author: Psychological-Key-36
replies.body: No one will ever play this game and very little amount of people will actually play fully vibe coded games. 2 prompt games are basically a game within the AI itself for the user to just create games out of thin air, but the chances of AI outputting a successful steam game have to be pretty much zero. The gaming experience here is playing a game that you just prompted out of pocket

replies.author: Abracadabroo
replies.body: Yeah, I'm vibecoding a game right now (mostly to see for myself if its possible) and I think making something quality is actually quite a bit of work still. Even if it nails coding aspects, claude still doesn't know shit about what is actually **fun**. I have to get very granular and spend hours to days on game balancing prompts and back and forth to make sure I am getting what I want. Nobody is making a steam game with 10 minutes of prompting

replies.author: carelessWhiskerr
replies.body: Doing the same, and agree with you on the amount of effort to get to quality. I see the distinction as hand-prompted vs hand-coded. Good game mechanics, story, art, etc is key to get right no matter how it’s built. But it’s incredible to be able to iterate and test ideas quickly with AI and pivot in real time. Still, I remain skeptical of the durability of the code… For now.

replies.author: daddywookie
replies.body:
Putting in a JSON based data layer so I could balance the game without AI interaction was an important step I have insisted on. I know when it gets to the pointy end that those numbers will be changing a lot.

It's very easy to let the AI take too much control.

comments.author: GrumpyPidgeon
comments.body:
This reminds me of when I was a technical architect for a digital ad agency and our client was evaluating a new content management system.  It demo'ed incredibly well, with them showing off their own web site with it and saying "we made this in three hours".  As engineers we cringed because we knew that the approach sells but doesn't build or maintain well in production.

The client loved it just as you would expect, and we were on the hook to implement and maintain.  It was a kludgy pain in the ass the entire way and we were perpetually fighting the client's perception that "they could make our web site in three hours, why are you struggling with this?"
